title: Initial-skill harm followed by evolved-skill gains is corrective adaptation, not a new self-evolution primitive
dead_end_scope: The standalone claim that MindMemOS's SpreadsheetBench transition from Init-skill below No-skill to evolved-skill above No-skill identifies a new agent-specific causal mechanism merely from the sign reversal or from supervised evolution adding more bounded rules.

fresh_phenomenon_closure.closure_scope: initial-skill negative transfer and corrective skill-evolution sign reversal only

counter_explanation.statement: The reported sign reversal is predicted by ordinary task-conditioned negative transfer followed by error-driven corrective skill optimization. MindMemOS's initial xlsx skill is a generic procedural artifact with sparse cautions and is worse than No-skill on SpreadsheetBench. Its unsupervised evolution turns recurring execution failures into concrete error-avoidance rules, while supervised evolution uses task scores to bound those rules and avoid overgeneralization, e.g. preserving requested formulas rather than hard-coding values merely to satisfy cached-value checks. SkillGrad independently reports the same qualitative object on SpreadsheetBench Verified across two backbones and two skill initializations: base xlsx skills can underperform No-skill, and failed plus contrastive-success trajectories are used as corrective evidence to patch the same skill into a higher-performing artifact. Therefore the negative-to-positive transition does not require an additional self-evolution primitive beyond skill-task misalignment, corrective learning, and rule specialization/applicability learning.
counter_explanation.opposite_prediction: Under matched executor, task distribution, skill initialization, feedback budget, and update capacity, held-out improvement should track how well edits correct task-relevant failure modes and constrain over-broad rules. An initially harmful skill can become beneficial when corrective examples remove or specialize misleading guidance; supervised counterexamples can further improve performance by learning when a rule should not apply. A generic prompt/skill optimizer with the same failed/successful traces and scores can express the same sign reversal without any special lineage, memory, or self-evolution variable.
counter_explanation.opposite_principle: Skill utility is conditional on task-artifact alignment; negative transfer from an unoptimized procedural artifact and its reversal through corrective rule specialization are ordinary adaptation phenomena, not evidence of a new self-evolution mechanism by themselves.
counter_explanation.opposite_search_seed: Search only for a preregistered residual where two skill-update procedures receive the same task-skill compatibility information, failed/successful trajectory evidence, task scores, edit/token budget, and held-out split yet make different ex-ante predictions about which task outcomes will flip sign. The residual must beat generic prompt optimization, error-driven corrective learning, positive-versus-negative concept learning, and nonmonotonic rule-revision baselines. Do not reopen from another base-skill-below-no-skill result or from merely adding applicability conditions.
counter_explanation.scope: MindMemOS arXiv:2608.12428v1 MindSkillEvolve evaluation and first-party repository commit 90491828726e1540442b17cd445d0308d0b8093c; SkillGrad arXiv:2605.27760v1 SpreadsheetBench skill optimization evidence.
alternative_explanations_ruled_out: The initial skill is simply neutral context: contradicted by both MindMemOS and SkillGrad, where base xlsx skills underperform No-skill on SpreadsheetBench.

MindMemOS evolution is only skill-length growth: contradicted by the first-party pipeline and Appendix B, which explicitly support add/revise/remove edits and show supervised boundary conditions that restrict over-broad rules.
The sign reversal is unique to MindMemOS: contradicted by SkillGrad's independent SpreadsheetBench results using two backbones and two skill initializations.

Task scores create an unidentified new mechanism: the supervised-only additions are applicability/exception boundaries and preservation constraints, directly expressible as counterexample-driven concept/rule specialization under the same feedback information.
counter_explanation.reopen_condition: Reopen only if a preregistered matched comparison equalizes task-skill compatibility, initial skill content, executor, failed/successful trajectory evidence, task-score information, edit/token budget, update count, and held-out evaluation, yet a self-evolution-specific structural variable yields a distinct ex-ante task-level sign-flip prediction that generic prompt/skill optimization, corrective learning, rule specialization, and nonmonotonic rule revision cannot express. More iterations, a different skill seed, a larger skill, or another negative-to-positive aggregate result is insufficient.

do_not_say: supervision does not improve skill evolution
scientific_interpretation.safe_claim: MindMemOS provides positive evidence that trajectory-driven skill refinement can turn a harmful generic skill into a useful task-aligned one, but the aggregate sign reversal and supervised boundary refinement are already explained by mature negative-transfer and corrective-learning objects.
